title.narrative: Early Recovery and Livelihoods for cyclone MOCHA-affected population

description.narrative:
ltpgt
lt/pgtltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-top:9.95ptmargin-right:0cmmargin-bottom: 9.95ptmargin-left:0cm"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtCyclone Mocha slammed into western Myanmar on May 14, 2023, as one of the strongest storms ever to hit the country, severely affecting over 1.6 million people. The cyclone’s winds at the speed of over 200 kilometers per hour (195 mph), made the landfall just north of Sittwe, tore over the Rakhine State destroying homes, bridges, boats, livelihoods, blocking roads, cutting communication lines, and damaging schools and hospitals. lt/spangtltspan lang="EN-US"gtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:9.95pt"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtRakhine Statelt/spangtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gt with a population of approximately 3.3 million, more than 80 percent live in rural villages where agriculture, fishery and aquaculture are the primary source of livelihoods. The storm flooded farmlands, lost seed stocks, killed thousands of livestock, and contaminating drinking water. Early assessment reports more than 50% of farmers lost their seeds stocks, which is going to have severe impact on food security and nutrition. Likewise fishing communities along the Rakhine coast were severely battered, causing extensive damage to fishing boats, fishing equipment and nets washed away by storm leaving the communities in despair. lt/spangtltspan lang="EN-US"gtlt/spangtlt/pgt
ltp class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom:9.95pt"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtUNDP is responding to cyclone Mocha through a dual approach or a combination of a rapid and early recovery response, and a long-term support for economic and social resilience of communities living in the affected areas. The funding support from the MHF will be channeled to support affected agriculture and fisherfolks to quickly restart their livelihoods, preventing total dependence on food aid, reducing burden on humanitarian agencies, and supporting affected communities to the path of recovery and resilience.lt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
